claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the gameplay involves completing everyday errands and tasks such as buying milk.

citations.review_text:
POSTAL 2 is the perfect game for when you want to spend a normal day doing completely normal errands in the least normal way possible.

The open-ended gameplay is what makes it so much fun. You can technically just complete your objectives, but the game constantly gives you opportunities to cause absolute chaos. The world reacts to your actions in ridiculous ways, and there's always some new way to turn a simple errand into a disaster.

The humor is crude, offensive, and definitely not for everyone, but if you're into that kind of dark, absurd comedy, there's a lot to enjoy. The NPCs, random encounters, and ridiculous weapons make the game feel like a playable collection of bad decisions.

It's old, janky, and definitely shows its age, but that jank is part of the charm.

**9/10 — went out to buy milk, somehow started a small-scale war.**
A calm walk in the park. I only came for the milk.

cohorts.summary: Reviewers progressing further find a structured weekly campaign with expanding difficulty and weapon variety.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight a wide variety of weapons and items, including a cat used with a shotgun, gasoline, matches, and various household objects.

citations.review_text: Don't take it too seriously and you might have fun with it. It's a good choice if you're looking for something silly where you can go crazy and not care about anything. You can kick, piss, burn and kill anything that moves. There are some stereotypes which one may find a little offensive, but like I said in the beginning of the review - don't take it too seriously. The description " It's only as violent as you are " is accurate because it's also possible to do a pacifist playthrough. I liked the variety/ originality (for some) of the weapons and that there are different ways to complete some of the tasks. Workshop definitely adds some replay value too.

Absolute polygon buffoonery.

You have to survive monday to friday, 5 days with various tasks. You can choose to be violent and commit atrocities like shoving a shotgun up a cat or mass shooting, or just be boring and pay for stuff. Most importantly, sheer freedom like pissing on taliban member's corpse or practically anyone in general, robbing a bank, acting as a cop, Playing catch with your dog using a human head, etc.

The main character, dude with receding hairline is a sociopathic character who could kill thousands and then himself before saying "i regret nothing". Throughout the game, he makes many enemies like the anti-game protesters, Tree huggers, rednecks, who proceed to shoot him the moment they see him.

The story is absurd. You do the most random BS. One moment buying milk, the other pissing on your father's grave. The game casually has racism and sexism which is pretty funny. If racism and stuff was not funny, top comedians wouldn't be using it. 

There are many weapon options, going as far as cow head, lighter and deodorant, Krotchy grenade, shotgun up a cat's ass, scissors, guns in general, so on. The game has extra content being special weekends.

I regret nothing.

Postal 2: O Caos em Estado Puro que Você Ama Incondicionalmente
Analisar Postal 2 hoje em dia é um exercício fascinante. Lançado em 2003 pela Running With Scissors, o jogo continua sendo um dos marcos mais bizarros, incorretos, caóticos e estranhamente brilhantes da história dos videogames. Ele é a definição perfeita do conceito de "plazer culposo", mas com uma camada de liberdade de game design que muitos jogos modernos de orçamento milionário têm medo de tentar.
A premissa: Uma semana na vida de um cara comum (ou quase)
A premissa não poderia ser mais simples: você é o Postal Dude, morando em um trailer na cidade fictícia de Paradise, Arizona, ao lado da sua esposa rabugenta e do seu cachorro Champ. De segunda a sexta-feira, você recebe uma lista de tarefas cotidianas absolutamente triviais para cumprir:
 * Comprar leite
 * Pegar o cheque de pagamento na empresa de jogos
 * Ir à igreja confessar seus pecados
 * Devolver um livro na biblioteca
 * Votar nas eleições
O toque de gênio da Running With Scissors é que o jogo nunca te obriga a atirar em ninguém. Teoricamente, você pode terminar a campanha sem disparar um único tiro ou matar uma única pessoa. O problema é que a cidade de Paradise é povoada por babacas, manifestantes violentos, fanáticos religiosos, caipiras insanos e policiais corruptos. A linha entre uma ida tranquila ao supermercado e uma guerra civil em escala urbana é tênue — e geralmente cruzada em menos de dois minutos.
Jogabilidade e A Liberdade do Caos
O loop de gameplay é um sandbox em primeira pessoa onde o humor negro dita as regras. O arsenal de Postal 2 é lendário e intencionalmente absurdo:
 * Silenciador de Gato: Sim, você pode pegar um gato de rua e usá-lo como silenciador para sua espingarda.
 * Lança-chamas e Gasolina: Espalhar combustível pela calçada e acender um palito de fósforo é estranhamente terapêutico.
 * Urinar a qualquer momento: O botão dedicado para urinar não serve apenas para piadas; serve para apagar incêndios no seu própr…

citations.review_text:
One of the funniest games i played in a while. This game is just an American simulator of a Dude living in Arizona just going out on his day tyring to find milk. Now where is that !? You can practicly do enything. You can rob a bank, brake out of prison, kill people in intersting ways, piss on people, people can kill you, you can hunt terorrists and make an Allah Akbar on a group of people protesting how violent videogames are. The game is great minus the constantly creshing at loading areas. Overall a great time really. Recomended.

8.5/10

This has to be the most unhinged game I've ever played. And yet I loved every second of it.

For starters, this game feared nothing. It's INSANELY controversial, pushing political correctness completely out the window.

I love the protagonist and his many voicelines. His deadpan tone and dark humor make him memorable.

You can PEE on the NPCs, and set off chain reactions with them. One time, there was a whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ world war going on because some idiot accidentally shot an other NPC instead of me.

The graphics are great for their time, but haven't aged well. The overall art design and visual humor still carry a lot of charm.

However, the gunplay is mediocre, the ending was very anti-climatic, and there was way too much walking for my liking. especially with those annoying loading zones between map sections.

Still though, this is an amazing game. But I'd steer clear if you can't handle it's controversial elements, because trust me.. there are A LOT.

citations.review_text:
One of the best games I've ever played, if you're reading this review buy it now, for full price, because you it is worth it and much more. Endless replayability after the main story. The main story may become slightly harder to get through during Thursday and Friday during the first playthrough but its all worth it to experience *enhanced mode*. Game worth £30 in my opinion but price only reflects age, which doesn't even affect gameplay as the game gets frequent performance updates for modern hardware as the devs care about people who play their games. This indie game has stood the test of time and aged like fine wine.

Also get postal 1 its free, it shares no resemblance with this game but its surprisingly good and free.
This game gets very hard IMO near the end of the game, but this is still the best postal game in the franchise. If you want to get into the postal series then this is a must play

cohorts.summary: Longer term players experience the escalation from chores to chaos while noticing some dated humor.

claims.claim: The game's humor and certain jokes have aged poorly over time.

citations.review_text: Very bad game, outdated humor, crashes a lot, and has a very repetitive gameplay: that being just shooting people with the most inaccurate weapons known in videogames' history (for no reason) and doing some stupid gruesome missions over and over again

This game embodies the word "chaos" like no other. It's absolutely incredible and an insane value if you can pick it up for under €1. Hell, it's worth paying full price, considering the amount of content it offers feels like ten times what you're paying for.

The game doesn't rely much on cutscenes or its story. They definitely add to the charm, but they aren't the main attraction. Picking up a paycheck or paying for a ticket wouldn't be interesting without the gameplay, Postal 2 lives and dies by the freedom it gives you. Being able to do almost anything you can imagine is a privilege very few games offer without it feeling forced or gimmicky. As ridiculous as it sounds, things like pissing on people or flipping them off don't feel out of place, and you even need to use them to complete certain tasks. It makes the game funnier, weirder, and more memorable

It's definitely not perfect though, some parts of the humor have definitely aged poorly. Nowadays, certain jokes feel more like corny Reddit humor than genuinely funny. Maybe that's part of the game's bizarre charm for some people, but it stood out to me. Even so, the city remains memorable thanks to the npc's, random events, and overall atmosphere, which made me go for a 100% in it. Listening to music while kicking around severed heads is weirdly entertaining if you can get past how corny the idea is.

Overall, this is by far the best Postal game. It's not the only good one, but Running With Scissors has never, and probably never will, reach the same heights again. Skip the donation to charity you were going to give with that €1 and spend it on this instead. Should be noted, making people twerk by pissing on them > buying "food" to "survive."

claims.claim: The game features a structure where the player completes mundane daily errands and chores that escalate into chaotic shootouts.

citations.review_text: this game is a top ten of all time for me, you play as a guy named Postal Dude and the main objective is that you have to do errands for your nagging wife (the ♥♥♥♥♥♥) like getting milk, going to get a Christmas tree (in july), pissing on your dads grave who may or may not be the postal dude from postal 1(thats just a theory, a game theory), and going to get people to sign your petition to make winy congressman play violent video games. There are 5 days and each usually has 3 to 4 tasks you have to finish. Sounds pretty mundane and boring right? well the fun part is that you can do these tasks as violently or peacefully as you want, a line in your way? pour gasoline on them and light them on fire! someone call you an idiot? piss on them! and plus postal dude seems to have a curse placed on him where wherever he goes s**t hits the fan and everything ends in a bloody shootout. there are a lot of places to explore in Paradise, neighborhoods, the trainyard, church, police station, and even a secret taliban base that you find by going through a secret tunnel behind the dude's trailer, after you go through the sewer you can raid the base and you can get an op super missile launcher. the only limit to where you can go is that some areas are locked until certain days. You can pretty much do whatever you want The gunplay is fun and simple and there is a large arsenal of weapons you can use, ranging from using a lighter and hairspray as a makeshift flamethrower, a m16, a 50 AE deagle, to a sycthe that you can throw and slice people in half with. The game runs very well but it crashes occasionally which is kinda annoying but since the game is from 2003 your computer will easily be able to run it. This is a game that i highly recommend to anyone to play and from my time playing it's been a very fun experience and I hope you enjoy it too.

Postal 2 is an absolute masterpiece of dark humor and unfiltered sandbox freedom, delivering a hilariously chaotic experience that remains unmatched in its sheer audacity. Instead of forcing violence on the player, the game brilliantly gives you mundane, everyday chores like picking up milk or returning a library book and lets you decide how to handle the escalating absurdity of a town gone mad. The weapon variety is delightfully unhinged, allowing you to use cats as silencers, pour gasoline on everything, or simply shock NPCs with your bizarre arsenal. Backed by its sharp political satire, memorable voice acting, and an open world that encourages pure, creative experimentation, it stands as an unforgettable cult classic that is a total blast to play.
